chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Musa narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan ibn Yazid, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The deed that is rewarded most quickly is al-birr (goodness/piety), and the deed that is punished most quickly is al-baghy (injustice/transgression). And sufficient blame is upon a man if he looks at people for faults while he is blind to them in himself, or he reproaches people for what he himself cannot refrain from, or he harms his companion with what does not concern him.'

key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Goodness, piety, or virtue; the opposite of sin.

ai.seo_question: What are the three character flaws that bring swift blame according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith links the rapidity of reward and punishment to the moral quality of *birr* (piety/goodness) and *baghy* (transgression/arrogance). It further defines sufficient blame (*‘ayb*) through three social sins: projecting one’s own hidden faults onto others, criticizing others for unavoidable traits, and causing unnecessary distress to companions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social etiquette (*adab*) and self-awareness.
